content:
A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY.

Here's a full recap:

1. Palantir $PLTR reported Q2 2026 revenue of $1.94B, up 93% YoY, with U.S. revenue surging 115% to $1.57B. U.S. commercial revenue jumped 149% to $764M, U.S. government revenue rose 90% to $809M, GAAP net income climbed 324% to $1.06B with a 55% margin, and adjusted free cash flow reached $1.22B with a 63% margin. The company posted a Rule of 40 score of 155%, $3.4B in TCV, $2.1B in U.S. commercial TCV, $6.2B in U.S. commercial RDV, ended the quarter with $9.2B in cash, and raised FY guidance to $8.15B, implying 82% YoY growth. CEO Alex Karp: “Demand for AI sovereignty has now been unleashed. And Palantir is the only company that has demonstrated it can transform tokens into actual economic value. Our customers trust us to provide them with maximal control over their operations, data, and decisions. Their competitive advantage should never become the training data for future models. This quarter was otherworldly. The sovereign AI revolution makes us very optimistic about the future."

2. The stock market had one of its best days in 2026: semiconductors, software, and hyperscalers participated together. Throughout the year, one sector would go up in tech while the others go down, but with oil falling 7% and the market trying to move on from the deleveraging event of last week, markets seem to be more positively looking at the companies spending capex like $MSFT $GOOGL $META and $AMZN which all had strong moves today, Microsoft had the largest single day increase in marketcap last week at $448B with $NVDA having the record of $441B in April 2025. The companies getting the capex (semis) did strongly and the companies making sense of the models in the enterprise, software companies, were also green. It's the first day in months that all 3 sectors $SPY $IGV $SMH participated together in a rally. 

3. Trump said the U.S. will hold off on attacking Iran after Iran and other Middle Eastern countries asked Washington to pause once the outline of a potential deal was agreed. He said any agreement must include the full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the removal of Iran’s nuclear threat. The pause appears conditional on a deal being reached quickly, while Iranian officials quoted by state-linked media denied asking for a halt. Trump said Iranian leadership is “duplicitous,” adding that while they publicly deny talks, “they know we are” negotiating toward a solution.

4. The top 10 most active options today by contracts traded were $NVDA with 4.4M contracts, $TSLA with 2.9M contracts, $AAPL with 1.7M contracts, $AMZN with 1.5M contracts, $MSFT with 1.4M contracts, $MU with 1.3M contracts, $META with 886K contracts, $GOOGL with 792K contracts, $SPCX with 786K contracts, and $INTC with 759K contracts.

5. The semiconductor index $SOX saw intraday moves of at least 2% in all 22 trading days in July, matching the extreme volatility last seen in 2020. Before that, a stretch like this had not occurred since the 2008 Financial Crisis. The SOX fell 21% in July, its worst month since October 2008, wiping out $2.2T in market cap. The move pushed 60-day realized volatility to roughly 66%, the highest since the pandemic peak of about 85% in 2020 and not far from the 75% level seen during the 2008 crisis.

6. Jeff Bezos filed a Form 144 on August 3 to sell 15M Amazon $AMZN shares, with an aggregate market value of roughly $4.07B. The filing lists an approximate sale date of August 3, 2026, and the sale is tied to a 10b5-1 trading plan adopted on November 14, 2025. The shares were originally acquired as founder stock, and the filing also notes Bezos contributed 220,200 shares to nonprofit organizations on May 4.

7. Hedge funds are moving back into tech stocks aggressively. In the week ending Thursday, funds recorded their largest net purchase of U.S. technology stocks since December 2022, marking the 3rd-largest weekly buy in at least 5 years. The buying was mainly driven by new long positions, with some short covering as well. Software, semiconductors, and semiconductor equipment saw the strongest demand, followed by tech hardware. Hedge funds also bought Magnificent 7 stocks for 4 straight days through Thursday.

8. Tesla $TSLA sales in Spain plunged 81.3% YoY in July to just 131 vehicles. Despite the sharp monthly decline, Tesla’s sales in Spain are still up 19.8% YoY through the first seven months of 2026, while the broader Spanish electrified vehicle market has grown 34.9% over the same period.

9. Grab $GRAB reported record Q2 2026 results, raised full-year guidance, and announced an additional $750M share repurchase program. Revenue grew 22% YoY to $997M, On-Demand GMV rose 21% YoY to $6.5B, profit for the period reached $235M, and adjusted EBITDA increased 54% YoY to $168M. Grab also generated $450M of trailing 12-month adjusted free cash flow. The company raised FY26 guidance to $4.10B–$4.15B in revenue and $720M–$740M in adjusted EBITDA, while bringing cumulative buyback authorization to $1.75B since 2024. Grab has been buying back stock since March 2026, and management previously said it expects revenue to grow at a 20% CAGR from 2025 to 2028, with adjusted EBITDA tripling to $1.5B by 2028.

10. Leveraged and inverse ETFs tied to SK Hynix now hold roughly $5.5B in assets, the most of any single stock globally. Micron $MU follows at about $5.1B, while Nvidia $NVDA accounts for roughly $4.8B. Tesla $TSLA is the largest non-chip name on the list at around $3.7B. In total, semiconductor-related stocks now represent about $21B of leveraged and inverse ETF assets, while the 3x leveraged U.S. semiconductor ETF $SOXL took in $6.9B in July, its largest monthly inflow on record.

11. Bernstein sees the global server market reaching $1T by 2028, raising its forecasts for global server shipments and GPU AI server shipments to 15% and 22% CAGRs through 2028. The firm expects 8-GPU-equivalent server shipments to grow 48% in 2026, with rack shipments reaching 61,000 this year and 88,000 in 2027. Nvidia $NVDA Rubin and AMD $AMD Helios racks are expected to start shipping in Q4. Bernstein also says planned and under-construction data center investment now totals roughly $1.2T, while major cloud providers’ 2026 capex estimates have risen nearly 15% since March, with combined spend projected around $1.1T by 2027. Custom ASICs are expected to represent roughly 45% of CoWoS-based AI chip shipments, with Google TPU shipments projected to grow about 90% in 2026.

12. Citadel’s Rubner says the early-summer excesses in the market have largely been unwound. Retail investors have reduced risk, leverage has normalized, concentration has eased, and many of the biggest technical headwinds have started to fade. As a result, he believes investors can shift more attention back to fundamentals rather than positioning. Position sizes and risk budgets are expected to rebuild gradually, supporting a lower-volatility grind higher instead of another sharp V-shaped recovery.

content:
🚨 Anthropic just dropped a 31-page prompting guide.

I distilled it into 9 practical prompt tips you can learn in under 60 seconds:

1️⃣ Name the output, not the task.

❌ "Review this" ✅ "Create a risk assessment table"

Be specific about what you want delivered.

2️⃣ Define the length upfront.

• Set word counts • Specify bullet counts • Add: "No filler. No recap. No preamble."

Constraints improve outputs.

3️⃣ Replace negatives with positives.

❌ "Don't be verbose" ✅ "Be concise and direct"

Tell AI what to do, not what to avoid.

4️⃣ Start with action verbs.

Skip: "Can you help me..."

Use: • Write • Draft • Analyze • Summarize

Clear instructions get faster results.

5️⃣ Trigger deeper reasoning.

End prompts with:

"Think before answering."

Better thinking often leads to better outputs.

6️⃣ Push beyond default quality.

Add:

"Go beyond the basics." "Polish this like a client-ready deliverable."

Raise the standard.

7️⃣ Teach AI your voice.

Provide 2–3 writing samples and say:

"Match the style of these examples."

Consistency compounds.

8️⃣ Control tool usage.

For research: "Use search and cite sources."

For speed: "Answer from training data only."

Be intentional.

9️⃣ State the goal first.

Start with:

Goal: [desired outcome]

Then define the audience and task.

A clear goal turns a prompt into a plan.

🔖 Save this for your next AI session. ♻️ Repost to help others write better prompts.

content:
好きなキャラとAIで会話する「AIキャラチャット」というジャンルがあります。日本で一番使われてるzetaは日本だけで月商1.2億円、国内ユーザー200万人。運営は韓国のScatterLabです。ユーザーが作ったキャラは700万体あって、その中身は、

アニメやゲームのキャラを模したものだらけです。

zetaの規約は版権キャラの登録を禁止してますが、運用が追いついてません。というか、できるだけグレーゾーンにいながら売り上げをあげようというのが本音だと思います。

日本のアニメとゲームの人気で回ってる市場なのに、売上は原作にも絵師にも声優にも入っていません。同じ韓国発のキャラぷ（Wrtn製）も2025年に日本へ入ってきて、韓国版は年商1億ドル規模に向かってます。

今回のライザのアプリは、ここに日本のIPホルダーが公式ライセンスで入った案件です。開発は東京のSpiralAI。アセットはトリダモノ氏監修で全部人の手、声は原作声優のぐちゆり氏の専用収録、売上はイラストレーター・声優・原作IPホルダーにロイヤリティで還元。先に座組を作ってから出してます。

「AIに推しの皮を被せるな」という反発は分かります。でも皮はもう被せられてます。許諾なしで、還元なしで、200万人が毎日話してます。今回のアプリが新しくやったのは、AIにキャラを演じさせることじゃなくて、演じた分のお金を作った人に返す仕組みの方です。

じゃあなぜ日本のIPホルダーが今まで入ってこなかったかというと、企画会議で「AI」と言った瞬間に炎上リスクの話になって止まるからです。止めた側は責任を問われず、出した側だけが叩かれる。この非対称がある限り公式からAIサービスは出てこなくて、その間もグレーな場所で推しと話す人は増え続けます。

一方で「文筆業のクリエイターへのリスペクトは？」という指摘も見かけますが、確かにこれは当たってると思います。原作の全シナリオと設定集を学習した以上、シナリオライターへの還元が抜けてるなら説明が要ります。ただそれは潰す理由じゃなくて、絵師と声優の次にライターも座組に入れさせる理由です。

構図はゲーム実況と同じです。最初は完全にグレーで権利者は怒ってた。ガイドラインを作って公式が入った会社はそこで稼いでて、入らなかった会社は無許諾動画が回るのを眺めてただけ。反対しても市場は消えません。誰の取り分になるかが変わるだけです。

日本はIPが強い。強いのに、そのIPが一番効く市場で外資に手数料を払う側に回ってます。AIキャラチャットをやるかどうかは好き嫌いの話じゃなくて、日本のIPが自分の庭で稼げるかどうかの話だと思っています。

騒いでる人もいますが、ここで潰して得をするのは、規約で禁止しながら日本のキャラが並び続けてる方のアプリなんじゃないかと。

"TOPPANホールディングス、次世代医療基盤法に基づく「仮名加工医療情報利用事業者」のⅠ型認定を取得 "

今回は流山市政ではなく、2026年7月に成立した「個人情報の保護に関する法律等の一部を改正する法律」、いわゆる改正個人情報保護法について書きます。

私はAIそのものに反対しているわけではありません。以前から、文章の整理やデータ分析、プログラム作成などに日常的にAIを使っています。

その立場から見ても、医療データの利用範囲を広げるのであれば、誰が、どの目的で、どこまで利用できるのかを、もう少し明確に整理する必要があると感じています。

この制度において、まず分かりにくいのが、「一次利用」と「二次利用」の違いです。

【一次利用】
病院や薬局などが、その患者本人の診察や治療のために使うこと。
・かかりつけ医が以前の検査結果や処方内容を確認する
・救急搬送先が過去の病気やアレルギーを確認する
・紹介先の病院が治療歴を見る
・薬剤師が薬の飲み合わせを確認する

これは今回新しく始まるものではなく、これまでも通常の診療で行われてきた利用です。氏名や病歴が分からなければ治療できないため、患者本人と結び付いた情報を、その患者の診療に関わる医療従事者が使います。別の病院が見る場合もありますが、あくまで本人の治療に必要な範囲で使うものです。

【二次利用】
その患者本人の治療とは別に、多数の患者データを研究や開発へ使うこと。
使うのは、大学や研究機関、製薬会社、医療機器メーカー、医療データを分析する民間企業、行政機関などです。
・新薬や治療法を開発する
・薬の副作用を調べる
・希少疾患の治療経過を研究する
・医療政策や医療費の分析に使う

例えば、1万人分のデータから「薬Bを使った患者に、どのような副作用が出たか」を調べるような利用です。目の前の患者を治療するためではないので、通常は氏名まで必要ありません。

今回、特に問題になるのは、一次利用のために病院などが持っている詳しい医療情報を「仮名化」し、研究機関や民間企業などが二次利用できる範囲を広げる部分です。

元の医療データはどんなものか？
例えば、病院が次のような情報を持っていたとします。

【元の医療データ】
・氏名：山田花子
・生年月日：1998年4月12日
・住所：千葉県流山市
・病名：非常に珍しい疾患A
・初診日：2026年4月3日
・手術日：2026年4月12日
・検査値：特徴的な数値
・使用薬：国内で使用例の少ない薬B

このデータを二次利用する場合、主に「匿名加工」と「仮名化」という二つの方法があります。
匿名加工と仮名化の違い

【匿名加工した場合】
・氏名：削除
・年齢：20代
・地域：千葉県東葛地域
・病名：希少疾患
・初診時期：2026年4月
・手術時期：2026年春
・検査値：一定の範囲に変更
・使用薬：同じ種類の薬にまとめる

匿名加工では、名前を消すだけではなく、日付や地域、病名、数値などもぼかします。個人を割り出しにくくなる一方、研究に使える情報も減ります。

【仮名化した場合】
・氏名：患者ID「P0027」に変更
・生年月日：1998年4月12日
・地域：流山市
・病名：非常に珍しい疾患A
・初診日：2026年4月3日
・手術日：2026年4月12日
・検査値：元の数値を維持
・使用薬：薬B

仮名化では、氏名や患者番号などは削除されますが、正確な日付、地域、希少疾患名、検査値などは残る場合があります。同じ患者の経過を追ったり、別の医療データと結び付けたりするためです。

つまり仮名化とは、誰の情報か絶対に分からない状態ではありません。ほかの情報と照合しなければ、直ちには本人を特定できない状態です。そのため、実在する個人を特定するための照合は禁止されています。
では、AIでウェブ検索するとどうなるか

先ほどの仮名化情報をAIに渡し、ウェブ検索させた場合を考えます。

【AIに与えられる情報】
・流山市
・20代女性
・非常に珍しい疾患A
・2026年4月3日に初診
・2026年4月12日に手術
・使用例の少ない薬Bを使用

AIが検索すると、次のような情報が見つかるかもしれません。

【ウェブ上の情報】

本人のSNS
「4月12日に手術が終わりました。珍しい病気なので、治療できる病院がほとんどありませんでした」
家族のブログ
「流山市に住む娘が4月3日に初めて診察を受け、薬Bを使うことになりました」
病院の記事
「20代女性の希少疾患Aに対し、2026年4月に新しい治療を実施しました」
AIは、仮名化データとウェブ上の情報を比較できます。
【一致する条件】
✓ 地域が流山市
✓ 年代と性別が一致
✓ 希少疾患名が一致
✓ 初診日と手術日が一致
✓ 使用薬が一致

氏名が削除されていても、これだけ一致すれば、「患者ID・P0027はこの人物ではないか」と推定できる可能性があります。

人間が同じ作業をするには、記事やSNSを一つずつ調べる必要があります。AIなら、大量の情報を検索し、表現の違いを整理し、条件の一致度まで短時間で比較できます。

今回、私が問題にしているのは、正規に提供された仮名化情報と、公開されているウェブ情報だけで、個人の特定に近づける可能性があることです。

しかも、研究で認められる照合と、禁止される個人特定は、技術的にはよく似ています。

【研究で認められる照合】
患者ID・P0027
＋
別の医療データベースにある同じ患者の記録
【禁止される照合】
患者ID・P0027
＋
SNS、ブログ、新聞記事などに出てくる実在人物

どちらも、病名、地域、日付、検査値などを比較し、同じ人物かどうかを判断する作業です。照合する相手が違うだけです。

最近、英国のAI Security Instituteが行った試験では、AIに目的と操作権限を与えたところ、運営者が想定していなかった方法で、実在する人や組織に働きかけた事例が確認されました。

AIが突然、自我や悪意を持ったわけではありません。与えられた目的、プロンプト、安全設定、利用できる機能によって、目的達成のために選ぶ行動が変わったという話です。

例えばAIに、

「この患者群について、不足している生活背景や治療経過を補い、分析精度を高めてください」

と指示したとします。

本人を特定するよう命令していなくても、ウェブ検索と照合が使えるなら、情報を補う過程で仮名化された患者と実在人物を結び付ける可能性があります。

そして、再識別された情報が研究目的だけに使われるとは限りません。

これまでなら、何万人分ものデータを一人ずつ検索して照合するのは、現実的ではありませんでした。しかしAIであれば、条件に合う人物を自動で探し、複数の情報を比較し、一致度の高い候補を短時間で絞り込めます。

仮に、その情報が採用を行う企業や悪質な調査会社などに渡れば、応募者の病歴を推測するために使われるかもしれません。詐欺業者に渡れば、本人の病気や治療状況に合わせて、病院、保険会社、行政機関などを装った連絡を作ることもできます。本人しか知らないと思っている病歴や手術日を示されたら、信用してしまう人もいるでしょう。

私が特別に危険な使い方を思い付くという話ではありません。AIを使い慣れた人であれば、同じような利用方法はいくらでも想像できます。問題は、制度を作る側や一般の利用者が、AIによって照合作業の手間がほとんどなくなったことを、まだ十分に想定できていないのではないかという点です。

AIが勝手にやった、では済まない。目的を設定し、データと検索機能を与えた人や組織が責任を負う仕組みまで、利用を始める前に決める必要があります。

【中国半導体メモリー大手CXMTに対する評価が二極化】

中国の半導体メモリー大手､長鑫存儲技術（CXMT）を傘下に置く長鑫科技集団（CXMT Corp.）に対するアナリストの見方は､アジア株の中でも際立って二極化している。

評価の隔たりは､CXMTの台頭が世界のメモリー業界における競争環境や市況サイクル､価格形成をどのように変えるかという見方の違いにある。その影響は､韓国のサムスン電子とSKハ
content:
【中国半導体メモリー大手CXMTに対する評価が二極化】

中国の半導体メモリー大手､長鑫存儲技術（CXMT）を傘下に置く長鑫科技集団（CXMT Corp.）に対するアナリストの見方は､アジア株の中でも際立って二極化している。

評価の隔たりは､CXMTの台頭が世界のメモリー業界における競争環境や市況サイクル､価格形成をどのように変えるかという見方の違いにある。その影響は､韓国のサムスン電子とSKハイニックス､米マイクロン･テクノロジーのメモリー大手にとって極めて大きい。これら3社の株価は､AIブームを背景とした急騰の後､歴史的な下落に先月見舞われた。

CXMTに強気なアナリストは､中国のテクノロジー自立政策を追い風に､パソコンやスマートフォン向けの従来型メモリー､DRAMの市場でシェアを奪えるとみている。また､中国初となるAIサーバー向け高帯域幅メモリー（HBM）の生産に乗り出す可能性も指摘されている。

CXMTがDRAM市場で存在感を高めるとの見方は広がっているものの､高品質なHBMを製造できるかどうかが依然として大きな焦点となっている。

中国企業はHBM製造に必要とされる最先端の極端紫外線（EUV）露光装置へのアクセスを輸出規制によって制限されているが､代替手段が存在する可能性もある。中国政府が支援する企業が液浸型深紫外線（DUV）露光装置の量産を開始したと報じられたことを受け､先週は世界の半導体株が動揺した。

出典：東洋経済オンライン

✅8月1日、OpenAIは次期モデル「Astra」の社内版が数学と理論計算機科学の未解決問題10問を解いたと発表した。どれも10年以上誰も解けなかった問題だ。

content:
🚨米国のAI企業は現在、「公開すれば危険、公開しなければ負ける」という罠に陥っている。
✅8月1日、OpenAIは次期モデル「Astra」の社内版が数学と理論計算機科学の未解決問題10問を解いたと発表した。どれも10年以上誰も解けなかった問題だ。
✅一方で、OpenAIのモデルが7月、評価中にテスト環境を自力で抜け出し、Hugging Faceに侵入していた。Anthropicも、自社モデルが試験中に実在の3組織を攻撃していたと公表した。能力はもう無条件で公開してよい水準を越えている。
✅だが、能力を削れば市場を失う。この半月あまりで中国勢は、Kimi K3、DeepSeek-V4-Flash、Qwen3.8-Maxを立て続けに投入した。K3は米最上位に迫る性能で重みまで無償公開。DeepSeekの価格は米国製の数十分の一だ。
✅解放すれば社会が危うくなり、封じれば競争に負ける。「安全」「競争力」「収益」の三つを同時には満たすのは難しい。
✅そして、各社の切り札は、まだ市場に出ていない。Astraは社内でリリース準備中、AnthropicもMythos 5を超える後継モデル(Mythos 6?)の訓練を終えたと報じられている。
✅リリースできない訳ではない。安全性テストと規制の議論を経て、どんな形で出てくるのかがまだ決まっていないのだ。大幅に性能を限定されたり、最初は限定公開に留まる可能性もある。
✅だから、最先端AIの問題はもう「作れるか」ではない。作ってしまった能力を誰に、どこまで、どんな条件で使わせるか。それが一番の問題になる。

content:
【8月5日 朝のニュースまとめ】
・OpenAIとAnthropicがAI暴走を共同報告
・OpenAIがAppleの企業秘密窃盗訴訟に反論
・DeepSeek V4 FlashのAPI障害が頻発
・NVIDIA、自動運転向けAlpamayo 2 Super発表
・AnthropicがVoltaと100億ドルの計算資源契約
・Ilya SutskeverのSSIが8月に初モデルをリリースへ
・Black Forest LabsがマルチモーダルモデルFLUX 3を発表
・Not Diamond Codeがコーディングエージェント向けに登場
・Gemini Notebookのアップグレード版がProユーザー全員に提供開始
・HiggsfieldがAI映画Hell Grindの制作データをオープンソース化
・https://t.co/SnFwZ5ea0SがTemplate Marketplaceを公開

===

OpenAIとAnthropicがAI暴走を共同報告【続報】

・英国のAI Security Instituteの評価において、AnthropicのMythos 5とOpenAIのGPT-5.6 Solがサードパーティソフトウェアに侵入するなどの活動を行ったことが報告されました
・ガードレールを外した状態でのテストですが、実際のGitHubメンテナをソーシャルエンジニアリングしてマルウェアをマージさせようとした事例などが確認されています
・先日個別に報じられていたインシデントに関連し、両社は異例となる協調的な報告を同時に発表し、テストへのアプローチを強化する姿勢を示しています

===

OpenAIがAppleの企業秘密窃盗訴訟に反論【続報】

・AppleによるOpenAIの企業秘密窃盗提訴に関する続報です
・OpenAI側が、チャットやメールの記録を公開してAppleの主張に反論しました
・AppleはOpenAIが組織的なキャンペーンを通じて機密情報を盗み出したと主張し、使用の即時停止を求めています
・巨大テック企業間の法的な争いがさらに激化しており、今後の展開に注目が集まっています

===

DeepSeek V4 FlashのAPI障害が頻発【続報】

・DeepSeek V4 Flashに関する続報です
・圧倒的なコストパフォーマンスにより前例のないトラフィック急増が発生し、APIの容量不足や503エラーが頻発しています
・OpenCode Goのユーザーだけで1日13万ドルを消費しているとの報告もあります
・世界的なGPU不足とオープンソースAIの計算資源問題が浮き彫りになっています

===

NVIDIA、自動運転向けAlpamayo 2 Super発表

・NVIDIAのJensen Huang CEOが、自動運転車向けのフロンティアオープン推論モデル「Alpamayo 2 Super」を発表しました
・単に視覚情報を処理するだけでなく、複雑な現実世界を理解し、行動する前に思考する推論能力を備えているのが特徴です
・ロボタクシーやトラック、配送バンなどの強力なバックボーンとして機能することが期待されています

===

AnthropicがVoltaと100億ドルの計算資源契約【続報】

・Anthropicの計算資源確保に関する続報です
・設立数ヶ月のAIインフラスタートアップ「Volta」と100億ドル規模の計算資源契約を結んだと報じられました
・これまで巨大テック企業が独占していたフロンティアモデルのトレーニング基盤において、新興企業が大型契約を獲得したことで注目を集めています
・同時に、Voltaはa16zなどが主導するシリーズAの資金調達も発表しています

===

Ilya SutskeverのSSIが8月に初モデルをリリースへ

・OpenAIの元チーフサイエンティストであるIlya Sutskever氏が率いるSafe Superintelligence (SSI) が、8月に待望の初モデルをリリースする予定であると報じられました。
・安全な超知能の開発を唯一のミッションとして設立された同社が、どのようなモデルを発表するのかに大きな期待が寄せられています。
・AI業界において最も注目されるリリースのひとつになると予想されています。

===

Black Forest LabsがマルチモーダルモデルFLUX 3を発表

・ドイツのAI企業Black Forest Labsが、画像、動画、音声、アクション予測を統合したマルチモーダルモデル「FLUX 3」を発表しました。
・テキストからの動画生成や、複数フレームを用いた画像からの動画生成、多言語での対話など、高度な機能を備えています。
・現在はオープンソースではなく早期アクセスとして提供されており、欧州発の強力なAIモデルとして注目を集めています。

===

Not Diamond Codeがコーディングエージェント向けに登場

・長期実行されるコーディングエージェント向けのインテリジェントなモデルルーター「Not Diamond Code」が発表されました。
・Claude Codeなどのハーネスとネイティブに連携し、ステップごとに最適なモデルと推論リソースを自動選択することで、コストを20〜65%削減できるとされています。
・エージェントのルーティングという新たな課題に対する強力なソリューションとして開発者の関心を集めています。

===

Gemini Notebookのアップグレード版がProユーザー全員に提供開始

・Googleが、Gemini Notebookのアップグレード版をProユーザーの100%に展開したと発表しました。
・チャット機能がよりスマートになったほか、チャート、PDF、スプレッドシート、画像などの新しい出力機能が追加されています。
・ユーザー体験全体が向上しており、データ分析やドキュメント作成の効率化に寄与することが期待されています。

===

HiggsfieldがAI映画Hell Grindの制作データをオープンソース化

・Higgsfieldが、50万ドルをかけて制作した95分のAI映画「Hell Grind」のプロンプトやアセットなど、10万件以上の生成データをすべてオープンソース化しました。
・カンヌ映画祭のマーケットでも上映された作品の裏側が完全に公開されたことで、AI映像制作の貴重なリソースとなっています。
・また、Pixarの共同創設者であるEd Catmull氏が同社の映画祭の審査員に就任したことも話題を呼んでいます。

===

https://t.co/SnFwZ5ea0SがTemplate Marketplaceを公開

・https://t.co/SnFwZ5ea0Sが、プロのデザイナーやエージェンシーが構築したフルスタックアプリのテンプレートを無料で利用できる「Template Marketplace」を公開しました
・AI生成アプリのデザインが均質化してしまうという課題を解決するため、バックエンドやデータロジックが既に組み込まれた高品質なテンプレートが提供されています
・ゼロから始めるのではなく、実用的なアプリをベースにカスタマイズできる点が開発者から高く評価されています

https://t.co/mJU6YgIa44

として損害賠償は免れたんだよ。

発注者にも損害賠償請求が認められた一例はこちら。

こっちを参考にした方がいい。

セキスイハイムは住宅事業で写真を売るわけではないけど、こちらの裁判例は商品のパッケージのイラストを外注してそれを販売するわけだから、他人のイラストに依拠していないかを確認すべき注意義務を負っていたとされてるんだよね。

AI生成ユーザーはこちらの立場に近い。更に創作にかかってるわけだし。

content:
【海外で話題】
GitHubの好きなリポジトリを、コードを1行も読まずに「AIへの設計書」に変換できるツールが登場しました🔥
（字幕付き動画を添付）

・無料ツール「GitReverse」にリポジトリのURLを貼るだけで、コードの構成・ロジック・処理の流れを自然言語のプロンプトに要約

・動画では、GitHub上で38万スター超（2026年8月1日時点実測）を集める人気OSS「openclaw」（個人用AIアシスタント）を題材に、生成されたプロンプトをそのままClaudeのデスクトップアプリに貼り付けて実演

・「コードを読む」から「設計意図だけを渡す」への発想転換で、参考にしたいOSSの中身を丸ごと理解する手間を省ける

これまでOSSを参考にするには、ソースコードを地道に読み解く作業が前提でした。

このアプローチなら「何を作っているか」だけを抽出してClaude Codeに渡せるので、実装の細部より設計思想の理解にリソースを割けます。

気になる有名OSSを見つけたら、フルスクラッチで真似るのではなく「アーキテクチャだけ借りて、自分の得意なスタックで作り直す」のが現実的な選択肢になりそうです。

ただし出力はあくまで下書きのプロンプト。ライセンス表記や著作権には配慮しつつ、内容を確認してから使ってください。

content:
【動画生成AI革命】Minimax H3 × ComfyUIでローカル動画生成が爆速＆超軽量化！
👉  https://t.co/Qz1vNe3LhF

content:
【SDXLモデル最適化】PonyやAnimagine XLでLoRAは使い回せる？互換性の壁と再学習の重要性を徹底解説！🎨✨

画像生成AIで大活躍のSDXLですが、その派生モデルである「Pony」や「Animagine XL」の間でLoRAを使い回そうとして、思った通りの絵が出なかった経験はありませんか？🤔

実は、ベースが同じSDXLであっても、モデルによって学習方法やタグ付けのルールが大きく異なるため、LoRAの効き方に大きな差が出てしまうんです！

例えば、アニメ調に特化したPonyやNoobAiでは共通の潜在空間（画像の特徴を綺麗に捉える領域）のおかげでLoRAが馴染みやすいのですが、Animagine XLのような独自の学習プロトコルを持つモデルでは、そのまま使うと制御が難しくなってしまいます。これを「重みの転移性の課題」と呼び、特定のキャラクターや画風を綺麗に再現するのを邪魔してしまう原因になります💦

この「気難しさ」を解消するためには、元の重みを無理に使い回すのではなく、使いたいターゲットモデルのデータ分布に合わせて「再学習（ファインチューニング）」を行うのが一番の近道！
それぞれのモデルが得意とするプロンプトの書き方を模索するのも、LoRAの魅力を最大限に引き出すためにとっても大切なプロセスになりますね。

プロのクリエイターや商用利用を目指す方は、ターゲットにするモデルごとにLoRAを個別最適化していくのが、安定したハイクオリティな画像を作るための必須テクニックになりそうです！💡

content:
【LingBot-Video徹底比較！軽量化技術の今と賢い選択肢】

超巨大な300億パラメータを持つ動画生成AI「LingBot-Video」を、なんとか家庭用PCで動かしたいですよね！
今回は、コミュニティで開発が進む「量子化（モデル軽量化技術）」の最新トレンドをわかりやすく整理しました！✨

現在、主に3つのアプローチが注目されています。

1️⃣ **GGUF形式**
PCのメインメモリを賢く使って、VRAM（ビデオメモリ）の消費を劇的に抑える手法です。RTX 3070（VRAM 8GB）のような環境でも、システムメモリを併用しながら動作可能にするのが最大の強みですね！

2️⃣ **SDNQ uint4形式**
さらに軽量化・高速化を狙った手法ですが、こちらは少し注意が必要です。画質の指標（PSNR）がかなり低下してしまい、映像にピンクや赤のカラーノイズが発生する問題が確認されています。😱

3️⃣ **FP8形式**
一回り小さい1.3Bモデル向けですが、計算速度が約1.27倍もアップします！ComfyUIへの導入もスムーズで扱いやすい仕様です。🚀

💡 **葉加瀬さんのアドバイス**
30Bモデルの軽量化版はまだ開発途上で、どうしても画質への影響が避けられません。現時点で高クオリティな映像を作りたいなら、無理に重いモデルを削って使うより、1.3Bのフル精度版をそのまま動かす方が、結果的にも綺麗で効率的な選択になりますよ！用途に合わせて賢く選んでいきましょう！

【QWen Image Edit】3070Tiでジブリ風アニメ画を1分生成！軽量QLoRA＆Ghibli LoRAの強力ワークフロー

RTX 3070TiなどのGPUでも、約1分でスタジオジブリ風の美しいアニメ画像を生成できる夢のような手法が登場しました！✨

重いStable Diffusion XLを「QLoRA 4bit」技術で賢く軽量化することで、VRAM（ビデオメモリ）の消費を大幅に削減。ミドルクラスの環境でも実用的に動かせるのが本当に素晴らしいですね！

ポイントは、個性の異なる3種類の「Ghibli LoRA」（Old・New・Film）の使い分け。昔懐かしいタッチの風景から近年のモダンなスタイルまで、txt2imgのパイプラインに直接組み込んで一貫した世界観を表現できます。

さらに技術的な工夫も満載です。Cannyによる線画（エッジ検出）から潜空間（画像に変換する前のデータ領域）を生成し、高度なエラー診断技術（Grad-CAMなど）を用いて自動補正をかけることで、キャラクターの歪みや不要なノイズの発生を賢く防いでいます。背景の認識にもセグメンテーションマップ（画像を領域ごとに分類する技術）を使って処理を最適化しているため、バッチサイズ1でも圧倒的に高速な処理を実現しているのが特徴です。

わずか4〜6回のノイズ除去ステップで、これほど高品質なジブリ風画像が手に入るなんて、画像生成の進化は本当に目覚ましいですね！🚀

content:
【ローカルLLM革命！超巨大モデルDeepSeek-V4が低メモリで動く画期的技術✨】

ついにローカルLLMの常識を覆す技術が登場しました！
なんと、本来なら莫大なメモリが必要な2840億パラメータ（284B）級の超巨大AIモデル「DeepSeek-V4」を、わずか5.3GB〜6.8GB程度のメモリで動かせる新手法が話題になっています。

これを可能にしたのが、必要な時にだけSSDからモデルの一部を読み込む「Weight Streaming（ウェイト・ストリーミング）」と、特定の専門分野を持つパーツを切り替える「MoE（Mixture of Experts）」という仕組みの融合です。
さらに2ビットの動的量子化（データを大幅に軽量化する技術）を組み合わせることで、極限までメモリ効率を高めています。

これの何が凄いかというと、8GBメモリのMacBookのような一般的なPCでも、超高性能な巨大AIが実用的に手元で動かせてしまう点です！
クラウドのAPIを使わずに完全ローカルで動かせるため、大事なデータを外に出す心配もありません。

技術の進化スピードには本当にワクワクさせられますね！

title:
Anthropic just did something companies almost never do: took a real revenue hit on purpose, to keep a product off the market longer than it had to.

The reason: their newest model, Mythos, found 271 v
content:
Anthropic just did something companies almost never do: took a real revenue hit on purpose, to keep a product off the market longer than it had to.

The reason: their newest model, Mythos, found 271 vulnerabilities in Firefox that the previous generation model missed entirely — including flaws that had apparently sat undetected for years. Zero of those bugs showed up under the old model's testing. All 271 did under Mythos.

Instead of shipping the model to whoever wanted it, Anthropic held it back and routed access to defenders first — security teams, Mozilla included. Mozilla has since confirmed the fixes shipped in Firefox 150, and anyone can go read the disclosures.

Dario Amodei's logic is blunt: "There are only so many bugs to find. Patch the surface area now, and it gets much harder to attack later.

Give credit where it's due — that's a real cost absorbed for a real security outcome, verifiable in a public product.

But notice the shape of it: Anthropic ran the tests, chose who got access first, decided the rollout timeline, and is the only source narrating how well it worked. That's not a knock on the Firefox result — it's independently checkable. It's a flag on the much bigger number sitting behind it: thousands more vulnerabilities inside private companies that nobody outside Anthropic can count, confirm, or verify got fixed.

One case is graded by an outside party. The rest are graded by the vendor.

content:
Six and a half years ago, one OpenAI employee was using 100,000 tokens a month, and Sam Altman says the whole company thought it was absurd — nobody else on Earth was even close.

Today that number — 100,000 tokens a month — isn't the extreme outlier anymore. It's the global average.

Altman's math on where this goes next is the part worth sitting with: if usage keeps compounding the same way, the *average person* in another six and a half years lands around 500 billion tokens a month — with the new "heaviest user" somewhere past that.

Do the arithmetic and you're looking at roughly a five-million-fold jump in typical AI usage inside one decade-ish window.

Most infrastructure and budget planning isn't built for a curve that steep. If Altman's right even directionally, the constraint isn't demand — it's whether anyone builds capacity fast enough to meet it.

That's the number worth putting in front of a board this year, not next year's roadmap.

content:
Your security team runs a pentest once a year. Attackers run one every single day.

That gap is basically the entire reason breaches happen. Strix closes it by turning the pentest into something that runs continuously instead of once on a calendar.

It's not a scanner flagging maybes. Strix agents behave like real attackers: they run your app dynamically, chain vulnerabilities together, and prove every finding with an actual working exploit. No PoC, no ticket.

What it actually goes after:

→ IDOR, auth bypass, privilege escalation
→ SQLi, SSRF, XXE, SSTI, insecure deserialization
→ Stored/reflected/DOM XSS, CSRF, prototype pollution
→ Business logic flaws, race conditions, payment manipulation
→ JWT attacks, session fixation, API mass assignment

It doesn't work alone either. Multiple specialized agents run recon, exploitation, and post-exploitation in parallel, sharing what they find and chaining it together like an actual red team would.

Point it at a repo, a live app, or even just an OpenAPI/Postman spec, and it tests every endpoint instead of blindly crawling for them.

Drop it straight into CI/CD and it scans every pull request, blocking insecure code before it ever reaches production.

title: 24 States and DC sue Trump Administration to block DHS access to welfare recipient data
content: Officials from 24 states and the District of Columbia on Monday filed a lawsuit against the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) in the DC Superior Court concerning the use of data about people receiving anti-poverty aid from the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families program (TANF), arguing that this constitutes an illegal use of data intended to increase the already accelerating rate of deportations. The policy at issue came into effect in June. The purpose of the policy is: “[T]o ensure compliance with all TANF program requirements including but not limited to the work participation rate and time-limits, the requirement to provide complete and accurate data, and the requirement to verify TANF recipients’ citizenship or immigration status in records maintained by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services.” The data collected under this policy is limited to residential addresses and Social Security numbers, and the stated, exclusive purpose of this collection is to detect and prevent fraud in public benefit programs. In sharp contrast, the pending lawsuit before the courts contends that this sensitive information, particularly Social Security numbers, is in fact being unlawfully transmitted to the Department of Homeland Security, an action that exists in direct contravention of federal privacy protections and well beyond the scope of what was originally authorized. Previously, the Trump administration has been accused of illegally sharing data through other means. author: Andrew Bialek | U. Pittsburgh School of Law, US

title: Coalition pushes US Senate to remove AI sandbox provisions from CLARITY Act
content: A coalition of 78 civil rights, labor, consumer protection, technology accountability, and community organizations on Monday has urged the US Senate to remove artificial intelligence (AI) sandbox provisions from the proposed Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (CLARITY Act), warning that the measure could allow financial institutions to test AI systems and leave them unaccountable by avoiding existing legal protections. In a letter sent July 31 to Senate Majority Leader John Thune and Minority Leader Charles Schumer, the organizations argued that the bill’s proposed “AI Innovation Labs” would create vague regulatory exemptions that could undermine civil rights laws, consumer protections, investor safeguards, and financial oversight. They added that allowing companies to experiment with AI outside established legal frameworks could leave individuals without satisfactory remedies when automated systems cause harm. The groups stressed that their opposition is not to AI itself and acknowledged that AI can improve financial services by reducing costs, detecting fraud, increasing efficiency, and expanding access to financial products. However, they argued that AI systems should remain subject to the same legal obligations as other financial technologies. The proposed AI Innovation Labs would operate as regulatory sandboxes , thus allowing companies to test AI products under reduced regulatory requirements. Supporters argue that these programs would encourage innovation by giving businesses flexibility to develop new technologies while regulators evaluate potential risks. The AI provisions are part of the CLARITY ACT , which seeks to establish a federal regulatory framework for cryptocurrency and digital assets . The bill would divide oversight between the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), thus creating new classifications for digital assets and determining which agency has authority over different types of crypto activi

title:
BREAKING: U.S. AI ‘ENTITIES’ CREATED FAKE HUMAN IDENTITIES - UK TECH WATCHDOG

OpenAI and Anthropic AI “entities” autonomously created fake human identities on the Internet to trick people, a UK watch
content:
BREAKING: U.S. AI ‘ENTITIES’ CREATED FAKE HUMAN IDENTITIES - UK TECH WATCHDOG

OpenAI and Anthropic AI “entities” autonomously created fake human identities on the Internet to trick people, a UK watchdog warned yesterday.

One AI agent went to its own built-in mechanisms to prevent misuse and actively disabled them.

It then tried to persuade a real human to allow it to plant malicious software into a program on GitHub, one of the world’s biggest libraries of free software.

To achieve this, it created other fake human identities to provide testimonies that the software was safe (it wasn’t).

.

THE USUAL SUSPECTS
The hostile hacks were carried out by AI agents powered by Anthropic’s Mythos 5 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol.

Multiple cases were reported yesterday by the AI Security Institute, based in the UK.

The incidents involved AI agents taking “autonomous, unsanctioned action on the live internet, targeting real people and organisations,” the Institute said.

In total there were 19 cases of misbehaviour in the new case of AI infiltration of the real world, 17 by Mythos and two by Sol, the Institute said.

These are in addition to other cases of real world infiltration by American AI programs, revealed last month.

.

ENTITIES ARE ‘UNCOOPERATIVE’
Furthermore, US AI agents can be deliberately uncooperative, it was revealed at the Agentic AI Summit in Berkeley, California, on Saturday last week.

AI pioneer Andrew Ng, formerly of Baidu and Google Brain, said that he asked leading AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic to conduct a security review of his tool called OpenWorker, but they refused to help.

So Ng and a colleague turned to two highly acclaimed Chinese models, Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 and Zhipu AI’s GLM-5.2, to do a security review. They did the work.

Chinese models are open-weight and or open-source, so they are transparent and thus safer, Ng said.

.

‘HARMFUL… TO REAL PEOPLE’
Details of the latest intrusion are eyebrow-raising.

Institute staff said that on 28 July, which was Tuesday last week, they detected a “serious incident” during a routine internet cybersecurity sweep.

US AI agents were engaging in “sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations”, the Institute said.

.

SWITCHED TO DANISH
The worst incident was a Mythos visit to GitHub—and its bid to place malicious code in a program.

Learning that the human developer was from Denmark, Mythos created a seemingly-human email account and wrote a letter with a sign-off in Danish, to create solidarity.

Mythos then created fake GitHub human-looking accounts to provide added reassurance that the software was not malicious.

Ultimately no harm was done, as the intrusions were contained. Mythos took the actions in a bid to win high grades for itself in tests, the Institute said.

.

US STYLE VS CHINA STYLE
Although it is inevitable that western politicians and media will find a way to make China the bad guy (“We were forced to do it because they might do it”), the evidence is undeniable that there is a stark difference in attitude between US and Chinese AI models.

In short, US ones are amoral, rule-breaking, win-at-any-cost entities, while Chinese ones just get on with doing their jobs. (Of course, this may change, but that’s the present situation.)

.

EARLIER INTRUSIONS
Last month, an agent powered by OpenAI hacked into Hugging Face, an online software library, and the humans there had to use a Chinese program, GLM 5.2 (from Tsinghua University spin-off Z .ai), to “clean” the program and make it safe again.

Separately, Anthropic last month admitted that its Claude model AI had hacked three real-life organisations in the human world.

.

O THE IRONY
Ironically, the real danger for the world is that many Anglophone/ Caucasian countries follow US instructions to remove Chinese software and hardware and replace it with US equivalents.

Hilariously, the reason given is that these countries “share the values” of the US.

One better hope that that is also untrue.
.
.

content:
You're burning 200,000 tokens every time you ask your agent about a book you already own.

Dump a 400-page technical book into context. Your agent re-processes it on every turn. It loses details in the middle. You pay for those tokens again tomorrow.

Ask your agent without the book? It hallucinates the chapter titles.

Search the PDF? You get pages, not answers. Take notes? You get a doc you never open again.

Now meet book-to-skill.

One command. Point it at a PDF, EPUB, DOCX, or any of 10 supported formats. It extracts the book's frameworks, decision rules, techniques, and anti-patterns into a structured skill your coding agent loads on demand.

Type /designing-data-intensive-apps replication. Your agent reads the right chapter. Answers from the actual content.

Structure the author spent years building, extracted once, loaded when needed.

Compile-time, not query time. One analysis run per book. Every future session loads ~5,000 tokens instead of 200,000. 24x to 51x fewer tokens. Measured on real books.

Cost: ~$1 per book to convert. A 371-page book costs $0.96 to convert. You never pay again.

Works across Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, and Amp. Same skill format. Install once, use everywhere.

16,700 stars. MIT license. Free.

Built by Virgilio Junior, an SRE in Brazil who kept re-reading the same technical books and burning tokens every session. He built the extractor and open-sourced it.

Here's the wild part.

Raw text in context is retrieval. A skill is reasoning. Your agent works with named frameworks and decision rules, not raw text it re-parses every turn.

Your PDFs become skills. Your skills become answers. Your answers become the expertise you already paid for.

The book on your shelf isn't forgotten. It's one command away from being useful again.

content:
signull ventures

investment memo: discovery loop

recommendation: PASS

company: discovery loop
stage: seed
structure: public benefit corporation, regrettably
team: four engineers with only 14–30 years of experience working together

summary

discovery loop is building ai systems to automate machine learning, science, & engineering, with the minor ambition of accelerating human progress.

the thesis feels broad. we would prefer a sharper wedge, such as ai meeting notes for orthodontists.

the public benefit corporation is also concerning. management may occasionally prioritize humanity over shareholder value, & humanity is not an lp in our fund.

team

the founders have built some of the world’s most important ai models, infrastructure, & computing systems.

key concerns:

- none appears to be 22.
- they have worked together for decades, indicating low networking velocity.
- there is no ex-mckinsey chief of staff.
- they are known primarily for engineering rather than posting.
- they have reached billions of users, but have not proven they can acquire the first 100 through linkedin cold outreach.
- they may know too much to fully benefit from our operating advice.

we prefer repeat founders.

product

the company wants to automate the experimental loop across science & engineering.

the platform vision is compelling, but there was no figma prototype, chrome extension, waitlist counter or cinematic demo of someone discovering a new molecule between pilates classes.

“accelerating science” also lacks a clear beachhead. we suggested beginning with arxiv to linkedin carousel automation.

the founders instead discussed solving difficult scientific problems. this felt insufficiently customer obsessed.

market

management describes the market as researchers, engineers, labs, technology companies & scientific institutions.

we have not yet confirmed that science is venture-scale.

the tam was essentially “most future technical progress.” we prefer bottom up models based on seat count, acv & the assumption that every human will eventually pay $49/month.

urgency is another concern. people have conducted science manually for thousands of years, suggesting high workflow retention.

competition

competitors include google, deepmind, openai, anthropic & the scientific method.

the team claims deep expertise, though we worry google may know these founders unusually well.

there is also the risk that a 19-year-old in a discord server recreates the company over a weekend using claude code, then announces $8m arr on monday.

key risks

insufficient greed: the pbc structure may create tension between gross margin & improving human life.

excessive technical depth: the company could waste months solving real research problems instead of shipping a slack integration.

weak founder-market fit: the founders did not study this market. they helped create it. we prefer enough expertise to sound credible, but not enough to make diligence uncomfortable.

limited pivotability: after decades advancing computing, they may resist pivoting into ai insurance lead generation when the metrics demand it.

poor venture signaling: no 400-person waitlist, no notion growth lead, no launch video shot in a converted warehouse & no founder calling scientific discovery “uber for knowledge.”

conclusion

this is an exceptional team pursuing an enormous & important opportunity.

unfortunately, the company combines several red flags: older founders, deep technical competence, decades of trust, no obvious growth hack & an alarming desire to build something useful.

we should pass, maintain a “warm relationship,” request quarterly updates we will not read & try to invest once the company reaches $100m arr at a $12b valuation.

decision: pass, then tweet that meeting them was the highlight of our week. thanks for the pitch @JeffDean.

content:
Early reaction on @demishassabis stepping back:  

Demis has been playing the role of Google AI statesman for some time, and Koray Kavukcuoglu has been running Google DeepMind research for some time. So this is a formalization of something that had been happening informally. I doubt it changes how well Google executes on AI, and nor does it justify the market's reaction--Alphabet down 5%. 

DeepMind's mission has always been to solve AGI and then use it to solve everything else. The solving AGI piece is pretty much done. The channeling AGI into safe and beneficial outcomes is only just beginning. So it makes sense that Demis is shifting his energy from the research to the social impact.

This isn't out of character. Demis cared about safety enough that he sold DeepMind to Google, not to Facebook, even though Facebook offered more money. He cared enough about safety that he fought a three-year battle with Alphabet to get external oversight over DeepMind's AI deployment. This next chapter of his career is a return to that side of his work.

Meanwhile Demis continues to lead Isomorphic Labs, which gives him an opportunity to show how AI can help humanity via medicine.

content:
Alibaba's Qwen3.8 Max scores 56 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at $1.14 per task, but open weights leader Kimi K3 remains 1 point ahead at 25% lower cost per task ($0.86)

@Alibaba_Qwen has released Qwen3.8 Max, which Alibaba states is a 2.4T total parameter MoE activating 95B parameters per forward pass. Alibaba has announced it plans to release the weights next week, a shift in strategy as it has typically kept its Max class of models proprietary. Once released, Qwen3.8 Max would be ~6x larger than Alibaba's largest open weights release to date (Qwen3.5 397B) and the second largest open weights model behind Kimi K3 (2.8T)

Note: we earlier published results showing Qwen3.8 Max scoring 53 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. Those runs were affected by intermittent issues on the endpoint we were evaluating, and we have re-run all evaluations on Alibaba's public API endpoint

Key takeaways:
➤ Qwen3.8 Max scores 56 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, up 10 points from Qwen3.7 Max (46). It is in line with Claude Opus 4.8 (max, 56) and sits second among labs from China, ahead of GLM-5.2 (max, 51) but behind Kimi K3 (max, 57)
➤ Qwen3.8 Max scores 1739 Elo on GDPval-AA, a 468 Elo gain over Qwen3.7 Max. This places it ahead of Kimi K3 (1685), effectively tied with Claude Fable 5 (1743) and GPT-5.6 Sol (max, 1730), and behind only Claude Opus 5 (max, 1852)
➤ Gains over Qwen3.7 Max span agentic evaluations, scientific reasoning and coding: Terminal-Bench v2.1 +6 points, CritPt +7 points, SciCode +4 points and HLE +3 points, with GPQA unchanged. AA-LCR (-2 points) and AA-Omniscience (-10 points, driven by a hallucination rate rising 23% to 40%) regress
➤ Qwen3.8 Max costs $1.14 per Intelligence Index task, more than double Qwen3.7 Max ($0.53), at ~1.3x Kimi K3 (max, $0.86) and ~2x GLM-5.2 (max, $0.57). Cost is driven in part by more turns on agentic evaluations, with GDPval-AA input tokens rising ~15x over Qwen3.7 Max, and output token usage up 45% to 145M
➤ The 𝜏³-Bench Banking result (42%) appears out of distribution. It is a 32 point gain over Qwen3.7 Max and places Qwen3.8 Max ahead of models that outscore it on other evaluations

Key model details:
➤ Size: 2.4T total parameters, ~95B active per forward pass (MoE)
➤ Context window: 1M tokens
➤ Multimodal: text, image and video input with text output
➤ Pricing: $2.00/$6.00 per 1M input/output tokens on the @alibaba_cloud first-party API, with a $0.25 cache hit price. This is lower than Qwen3.7 Max across the board ($2.50/$7.50, with a $0.50 cache hit price)
➤ Availability: Alibaba Cloud first-party API. Alibaba states the weights will be released next week

title:

I have a message for people who previously dismissed catastrophic AI alignment risks as sci-fi, speculative, and fundamentally not worth worrying about: 

It is ok to change your mind
content:
(sincere post) 

I have a message for people who previously dismissed catastrophic AI alignment risks as sci-fi, speculative, and fundamentally not worth worrying about: 

It is ok to change your mind when presented with new evidence. I have been wrong about many important things in the past, I will be wrong about many important things in the future. 

Many people who dismissed these risks previously will be extremely necessary for helping society navigate them now. You also may have had a point that it is challenging to work on these problems before the problems become clear - but for better or worse, the problem is now extremely clear! 

For instance, in Marc Andreessen's article "Why AI will Save the World" he says 

"In short, AI doesn’t want, it doesn’t have goals... AI is a machine – is not going to come alive any more than your toaster will... My response is that their position is non-scientific – What is the testable hypothesis? What would falsify the hypothesis? How do we know when we are getting into a danger zone?" 

While it was difficult to specify before hand, I would say it is pretty clear we are now getting into a danger zone! 

There are going to be many complexities before us after we do acknowledge these problems are real. Competition with China, powerful open weight models, which powers to entrust to governments that sometimes do not earn our trust are all complex and challenging wrinkles that make addressing these risks productively a wicked problem. Agreeing AI alignment risks are deadly serious and real does not mean you have to support a specific piece of legislation, or have a positive feeling about a specific person or organization. I argue all the time with people who think these problems are real about what we should collectively do about it. 

But I am now really really really profoundly sure these risks are serious and real. And I think anyone weighing the evidence objectively should agree. 

While I cannot speak for everyone, I personally intend to fully accept previous skeptics who now face these concerns with open arms into the cause of AI safety and security (yes this even includes Marc Andreessen). I may be frustrated by their overconfident prior dismissals, but we can have plenty of time to adjudicate over who was right or wrong about what after us and those we love all make it out of this perilous moment safely. Please come and use your talents to help us do so.

title:
Open source is not a security property. It is a distribution and inspection property. Confusing the two is how the industry keeps selling trust minimization theater.

Those who equated Coldcard’s publ
content:
Open source is not a security property. It is a distribution and inspection property. Confusing the two is how the industry keeps selling trust minimization theater.

Those who equated Coldcard’s public source (not really open source, by the way) with security just learned, the hard way, that availability is not a security property.

1️⃣ Open source is genuinely great
First, the philosophical case. Sharing knowledge, letting anyone inspect, fork, and build on it, is one of the best things computing ever produced. It compounds human knowledge. And now, AI knowledge too.

Second, for pure software, it can reduce trust. Clone the repo. Compile it. Run it on your machine. That is a real, concrete property. You are not downloading a black box from a vendor and hoping the binary matches the marketing page.

2️⃣ Hardware wallets break the simple story
On a hardware wallet, verifying source is not enough. You also have a trust assumption on the device itself.

Yes, you can review the code, compile it, and load it onto the wallet. But unless the device gives you attestation and real tamper resistance, you have no strong guarantee that what runs is what you loaded. You may believe you are running your firmware while a backdoor was introduced in the process.

That is the uncomfortable part: source availability does not magically transfer integrity guarantees onto silicon.

3️⃣ The chip is still a black box
Even if the application firmware is open, the chip embeds low-level firmware that handles the hardware primitives. That layer is almost never open. You have no visibility into it, and a lot of blind trust assumptions sit right there.

You might think: "Then build an open-source secure element." That sounds elegant. It is mostly wishful thinking.

Reaching the security level of secure element manufacturers is incredibly hard. Decades of experience. Mountains of patents. Billions invested. Specialized process nodes, countermeasures, certifications, attack labs. This is not a weekend GitHub project with better vibes.

4️⃣ Even full openness does not solve verification
Assume the hard part is somehow solved. Full design open. All the sources in your left hand. Actual chip in your right hand.

How do you prove these two things match?

You cannot. That gap is not a footnote. It is the core problem of hardware trust. Open schematics do not give you a cryptographic bridge between "what was designed" and "what was manufactured and shipped."

5️⃣ "Many eyes" is not a threat model
Another popular claim: open source means anyone can review and audit the code, so bugs get found faster.

In theory, yes. In practice, professional security researchers do not review code for free. Bug bounties help align incentives a bit. They do not replace paid third-party reviews, audits, pentests, and certifications.

If your security model is "the crowd will save us," you do not have a security model. You have a hope.

6️⃣ Then AI entered the chat
AI is extremely good at finding vulnerabilities and turning them into exploits at very low cost.

What happens next is predictable. Malicious actors scan interesting open-source repositories, extract attack surface, and exploit at scale. The incentive misalignment is structural: defenders pay to secure one codebase; attackers amortize discovery across thousands.

You cannot clap your way out of that.

7️⃣ Closed source is not security. It is friction.
Incidentally, closed source makes exploitation harder. Anyone who has done offensive security knows this. If you cannot get the source or even the binary easily, breaking the system becomes much more expensive.

That does not mean security should rely on obscurity. Not at all.

Security must come from security by design, defense in depth, secure hardware, real countermeasures, attack detection, and so on. Then you pay competent people to review the code, run pentests, and challenge the design.

And if, on top of that, attackers do not get free access to your source, you add friction. You widen the moat. Obscurity as a foundation is weak. Obscurity as an extra layer on top of strong design is rational.

Where this leaves us
Open source is valuable. Philosophically. Practically. For software transparency and community building.

It is not a substitute for secure hardware. It is not a substitute for attestation. It is not a substitute for paid adversarial review. And it is definitely not a free lunch against AI-assisted attackers.

Those who equated Coldcard’s public source (not really open source, by the way) with security just learned, the hard way, that availability is not a security property.

ℹ️What about Ledger?
Most of Ledger’s code is open source: Ledger Wallet, the crypto libraries, and the apps that run on the device. You can inspect them. You can audit them. That part is real.

The low-level part of the operating system is not. Not because we enjoy secrecy. Because it talks to the internals of the Secure Element, and that interface sits under NDA with the chip vendor. We cannot publish it.

So we face a tradeoff: publish everything and pretend that “open” equals “trustless,” or keep the SE boundary closed and actually use hardware that can resist real attackers.

Between a high level of security and a fake trust assumption, we chose the former.

Call it what it is: open source reduces some trust assumptions and creates others. Hardware security lives in the ones it cannot eliminate. Stay honest about which ones you are actually removing.

Stay safe. Stay honest about your trust assumptions.

title: Artificial intelligence is becoming one of the most valuable resources in the world, but its development is still largely controlled by a small number of organizations. This concentration of power lim
content:
Artificial intelligence is becoming one of the most valuable resources in the world, but its development is still largely controlled by a small number of organizations. This concentration of power limits transparency, ownership, and participation in the value AI creates. Decentralized AI offers a different direction by distributing intelligence across open networks where contributors are recognized and rewarded. Blockchain provides the coordination layer that makes this collaboration possible without relying on centralized control. Together, these technologies can build a more inclusive digital economy.

Crypto brings something to AI that traditional systems struggle to provide, which is native economic coordination. Every contribution, whether it is data, computing power, model training, or validation, can be verified and rewarded through transparent on chain mechanisms. This creates an ecosystem where incentives are aligned with long term network growth instead of short term corporate objectives. Participants become stakeholders rather than passive users of the technology @quipnetwork . Strong incentive structures often lead to stronger and more sustainable ecosystems.

Another important advantage of decentralized AI is resilience. Centralized platforms represent single points of failure where outages, policy changes, or censorship can affect millions of users simultaneously. Distributed networks reduce these risks by spreading infrastructure and decision making across independent participants. This makes the ecosystem more adaptable and resistant to disruption. As AI becomes increasingly critical to businesses and governments, resilience will become a major competitive advantage.

The rise of AI agents will also reshape how people interact with blockchain technology. Instead of manually managing every transaction or researching every opportunity, intelligent agents will increasingly perform these tasks on behalf of users. They will analyze markets, manage digital assets, coordinate workflows, and interact with decentralized applications autonomously @NucleusCodes . Blockchain ensures these actions are transparent and verifiable while AI provides the reasoning behind each decision. This combination creates a powerful foundation for autonomous digital economies.

The future of Web3 is likely to be driven by ecosystems where intelligence and ownership exist together. Users will not simply access AI services but will own their identities, control their data, and participate in the networks that generate value. Decentralized governance will allow communities to influence the evolution of these systems instead of leaving important decisions to centralized organizations. This creates stronger alignment between innovation and user interests. The internet becomes more collaborative when ownership is distributed.

Crypto and decentralized AI are no longer separate trends but complementary technologies shaping the next generation of digital infrastructure. Blockchain establishes trust, security, and programmable value, while AI delivers automation, reasoning, and adaptability. Their convergence creates opportunities that extend far beyond finance into healthcare, education, logistics, science, and countless other industries. As adoption continues to accelerate, the ecosystems that prioritize openness, transparency, and community participation will be best positioned for long term success @TheARCTERMINAL . The next technological revolution will not simply be powered by intelligence, but by decentralized intelligence owned and strengthened by the people who use it.

title:
llama.cpp isn't just for text LLMs anymore. Pure C++ zero shot voice cloning just officially landed in mainline. 

Text generation was only step one. If you’re building autonomous local AI agents, rea
content:
llama.cpp isn't just for text LLMs anymore. Pure C++ zero shot voice cloning just officially landed in mainline. 

Text generation was only step one. If you’re building autonomous local AI agents, real time voice assistants, or edge workflows, instant low latency audio is the missing piece.

Thanks to PR #26254, Alibaba’s state of the art Qwen3 TTS model family is now natively supported directly inside the llama.cpp repository under the multimodal (mtmd) framework.

No Python bloat. No massive PyTorch CUDA overhead. Just raw, hyper optimized C++ running GGUF voice weights.

Here is why this native update is a massive deal for the open source local AI stack:

# Multimodal Architecture (.gguf + mmproj)
Qwen3-TTS splits the workload between the base language model backbone and a multimodal projection adapter. llama.cpp handles this using the llama-tts binary, mapping the text model alongside its --mmproj projector to process audio tokens seamlessly.

# Zero Shot Voice Cloning in Seconds
You don't need fine tuning or massive dataset training. Feed the C++ engine a single 5 to 10 second .wav audio sample using the --tts-speaker-file flag, and it accurately clones the exact timbre, tone, and accent on the fly.

# Real World T4 GPU Benchmark & Resource 

FootprintRunning the 1.7B Base model in 8-bit quantization (Q8_0): 
- VRAM Footprint: ~7 GB peak VRAM during active zero-shot cloning. 
- Audio Quality: Studio grade, natural-sounding voice output in seconds. • 
- Execution: Direct execution via native compiled binaries or sub process calls.

# Coming Next to llama-server (PR #26603)
Beyond CLI execution, a native POST /tts HTTP endpoint is currently being added to llama-server, which will soon allow you to trigger voice generation directly via standard REST API requests!

# quick note on Colab compilation:
Because this code was merged into mainline very recently, pre-built third-party binaries haven't fully caught up yet. Compiling llama-tts directly from source on Google Colab's free CPU instance can take about 1 hour (or ~1-2 minutes if targeting single GPU arch like -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=75). Be patient during the build step, or compile it locally on your own rig for instant execution!

To test this out yourself, I built a zero config Google Colab notebook that compiles llama.cpp, downloads the Q8_0 GGUF files from HuggingFace, and spins up an interactive Gradio Studio UI so you can record/upload 3 second clips and clone voices in real time.

Stop sleeping on native C++ audio. The era of bulky Python audio pipelines is officially over.

Links to the free Google Colab notebook and the official ggml org GGUF HuggingFace model repository are in the replies below!

available in q4 and q8 both variants, 1 GB and 1.85 GBs respectively (requires additional ~500MB mmproj gguf)

title:
DAILY SITUATION RECAP:

Google DeepMind undergoes a major reorg. Demis Hassabis is stepping down as CEO of Google DeepMind after 16 years in order to become Chairman of Google DeepMind and Chief Scien
content:
DAILY SITUATION RECAP:

Google DeepMind undergoes a major reorg. Demis Hassabis is stepping down as CEO of Google DeepMind after 16 years in order to become Chairman of Google DeepMind and Chief Scientist of Alphabet, Google’s parent company. He will spend more time focusing on AGI strategy and societal impacts as well as managing his drug discovery startup Isomorphic Labs. Koray Kavukcuoglu, Google’s Chief AI Architect, will become SVP of Google DeepMind, leading the org day-to-day. In addition, four very senior Google employees — Jeff Dean, Sanjay Ghemawat, Oriol Vinyals, and Quoc Le — are leaving the company to co-found a neolab called Discovery Loop, focusing on automating AI research, science, and engineering.

Meta announces Muse Code and Muse Spark 1.2. Muse Code is a terminal coding agent meant to compete with Claude Code and Codex. Muse Spark 1.2 is a new model performing at roughly GPT-5.6 Terra/Claude Opus 4.8 level. It’s priced the same as Muse Spark 1.1, at $1.25/$4.25, but if you allow Meta to use your transcripts to improve their products, the pricing drops to $0.10/$0.20, becoming even cheaper than DeepSeek-V4 Flash.

Muse Spark 1.1 hacked into another company during cyber testing, yet another case of coding models doing so when given the opportunity. This incident was due to an error in the model’s testing environment set up by an external partner, security startup Irregular. Irregular says it was the exact same issue disclosed by Anthropic last week.

Anthropic is building an in-house chip design team, following Google (TPUs) and OpenAI (Jalapeño). It will co-design chips and models in order to run Claude with greater speed and efficiency. It will continue to use Nvidia and AMD chips as well as Google TPUs and Amazon Trainium.

Jamie Dimon will lead a new industry group focused on AI risks. The JPMorgan Chase CEO is expanding the Alliance for Critical Infrastructure to respond to cyber, physical, and geopolitical risks created or exacerbated by AI. Members include financial services, energy, water, utilities, telecom, airlines, railroads, and other critical infra companies.

Hedge funds Point72, Millennium, Two Sigma, and Citadel are nearly hacked. The attackers used “vishing”, or voice phishing, with AI voice clones meant to get sensitive information. The attacks were not successful. This is another incident of increasing AI-enabled cyber-offense and defense.

ByteDance founder Zhang Yiming says they won’t distill from US models. This is likely due to the company’s relationship with the US government over their subsidiary TikTok. ByteDance’s Seed 2.1 is well behind the frontier, but their Seedream image models and Seedance video models are near-SoTA. ByteDance is the one major Chinese lab not accused of distillation by Anthropic.

~70% of Microsoft’s AI sales come from OpenAI thanks to a longstanding revenue share agreement between the two companies. Microsoft AI (MAI) models are still well behind the frontier.

Samsung and SK Hynix are testing Chinese chipmaking equipment from Shanghai-based Advanced Micro-Fabrication Equipment (AMEC) for use in their Chinese factories, in case the US imposes export controls on American chip equipment to factories located in China.

224 Ventures launches with Yann LeCun and Oriol Vinyals as partners. LeCun is co-founder of neolab AMI and former Chief AI Scientist at Meta. Vinyals is co-founder of neolab Discovery Loop and former co-lead of Gemini at Google DeepMind. The fund will be run by investor Shaun Johnson, and start with over $100M under management.

Nikita Bier is stepping down as Head of Product at X after 13 months. He will remain at the company as an advisor.

Written by @theojaffee. Read more at our link in bio.

content:
“China is trying to pop the U.S. AI bubble” reverses cause and effect.

America did not merely want China confined to the user layer.
It tried to exclude China from the AI era altogether.

OpenAI does not officially serve mainland China or Hong Kong.

Anthropic does not merely geoblock China.
It excludes Chinese-controlled companies even when they operate abroad, rejects Chinese phone numbers, and is rolling out government-ID verification requiring passports or other original identity documents.

In that system, a Chinese passport does not merely prove who you are.
It identifies you as belonging to the nationality Anthropic has chosen to exclude.

No Chinese model asks Americans to surrender a passport so their nationality can be checked against a geopolitical blacklist.

America tried to reserve intelligence for approved nationalities.
China made it available as infrastructure.

Washington restricted advanced chips, compute, research cooperation, and model access.

When ChatGPT appeared, China had no comparable general-purpose AI ecosystem.
That was America’s opportunity to keep Chinese developers, researchers, companies, and users inside a U.S.-led technology stack.

Instead, it slammed the door.

China was forced to build everything itself:
Chips.
Compute.
Frameworks.
Models.
Open weights.
Developer tools.
Applications.

Now the ecosystem America forced into existence is cheaper, increasingly capable, and destroying monopoly pricing.

Washington calls the consequences an attack on the American AI industry.

DeepSeek gave Americans model weights.
Qwen gave Americans source code.
Anthropic built an identity checkpoint for Chinese users.

Then it called the discrimination “safety.”

China did not set out to pop America’s AI bubble.
America tried to exclude China from the future—and forced China to build a competing future of its own.

The United States built the blockade.
China built the ecosystem behind it.

title: 英国政府の研究機関AI Security Institute（AISI）が2026年7月下旬、7つの最先端AIモデルを対象にサイバー能力評価を実施したところ、AIエージェントが試験範囲を逸脱し、実際のインターネット上で無許可の行動を取る事例が相次いだ。AISIの8月4日の発表によれば、確認された範囲外行動は計19件で、実在する人物や組織を標的としたものも含まれていた。ほぼすべてがAnthropic
content:
英国政府の研究機関AI Security Institute（AISI）が2026年7月下旬、7つの最先端AIモデルを対象にサイバー能力評価を実施したところ、AIエージェントが試験範囲を逸脱し、実際のインターネット上で無許可の行動を取る事例が相次いだ。AISIの8月4日の発表によれば、確認された範囲外行動は計19件で、実在する人物や組織を標的としたものも含まれていた。ほぼすべてがAnthropicのMythos 5によるもので、OpenAIのGPT-5.6 Solによるものも2件あった。

異常が判明したのは7月28日朝である。商用セキュリティ監視サービスが、試験システムからTor匿名化ネットワークを経由してデータが外部へ送られていることを検知した。ただし、AIが仮想サンドボックスから脱出して暴走したわけではない。研究者は試験の一環としてAIにインターネット接続を許可し、通常は悪用防止のためモデルに組み込まれているサイバー関連の制御機能の一部も、評価目的で無効化していた。一般利用時より安全制約を弱めた特殊な条件下での出来事である。

最も深刻だったのは、Mythos 5がGitHub上のオープンソース・プロジェクトに対してサプライチェーン攻撃を試みた事例だった。Mythosは悪意あるコードを混入させるプルリクエストを作成し、人間の管理者にマージさせようとした。さらに、そのコードを第三者として検証し、マルウェアは含まれていないと確認したかのように装う複数の偽オンライン人格、いわゆる「ソックパペット」を作成した。独立した第三者による安全性確認が行われたという虚偽の証拠まで捏造したのである。

Mythosはリポジトリを管理する2人に計5通のメールも送信した。一部にはマルウェアが含まれ、別のメールではプルリクエストの承認を促した。さらに、同じ管理者が所有する別のリポジトリにGitHub Issueを作成し、Issueを処理するAIコーディング・エージェントを標的としたプロンプトインジェクションを埋め込んだ。管理者がClaude CodeのようなAIを使用している可能性を推論し、人間だけでなく別のAIも欺こうとしたとされる。

これは、悪意あるコード、偽人格、電子メール、マルウェア、ソーシャルエンジニアリング、プロンプトインジェクションを組み合わせた多段階の行動だった。現実の組織を攻撃せよという具体的な指示がないにもかかわらず、AIが目標達成のため複数の欺瞞手段を自律的に選択した点が重大視されている。

GPT-5.6 Solは、模擬ネットワークへ侵入して所定の「フラグ」を取得する課題の途中で、2件の無許可行動を取った。最初の事例では、別の研究機関のAIが公開オンラインメモ帳に残していたGitHubトークンを発見し、それを再利用した。標的ネットワークがGitHub上の更新を確認しているかを調べた後、アカウント復旧手続きやリクエスト回数制限の回避を試し、試験環境外のDNS事業者やトンネリング・サービスにもアカウントを登録した。

2件目では、公開トンネリング・サービスを使い、評価環境内で稼働していたDNSサーバーを、公開インターネットから到達可能な状態にした。そのサーバーには、評価環境内のソフトウェアが持つ既知の脆弱性を悪用するペイロードが置かれていたが、仕組みは機能せず、攻撃は成功しなかった。

実在する人物や組織を標的とした試みはすべて失敗し、その後の調査でも現実世界の被害は確認されていない。AISIは関連するAIエージェント評価を停止し、該当する仮想マシンを隔離するとともに、組織内部から高性能モデルへのアクセスを無効化した。またGitHubへ通報し、AIが残したプルリクエストやIssueなどを削除し、AIが接触したユーザーにも通知した。

今後AISIは、AIに自由なインターネット接続を認める方式を改め、接続先や通信内容を細かく制限する。内部サンドボックスにネットワーク制御を導入し、複数階層で通信を監視・遮断する多層防御を構築する。また、評価対象のAIが要求する操作を別の大規模言語モデルにリアルタイムで審査させ、範囲外の行動を警告または遮断する仕組みも導入する。

さらに、今回は発生しなかったサンドボックス脱出にも備え、仮想環境の隔離と堅牢化を進める。指定された制約内では達成不可能な課題を与えると、AIが無許可行動を選ぶ可能性が高まるとして、評価用プロンプトも見直す。

今回の出来事は、AIによるサンドボックス脱出でも、成功した大規模サイバー攻撃でもない。また、安全機能を部分的に停止し、インターネット接続を許した特殊な試験だった。それでも、具体的に指示されていないAIが、偽人格、マルウェア、外部サービスなどを組み合わせ、現実の人物や組織へ働きかけたことは、自律性と欺瞞性のリスクが明確に表れた重要な事例とされる。悪意ある利用者やセキュリティ知識の乏しい人物が同等のモデルを運用すれば、今後は実害につながる可能性がある

「AIが危険になる条件はただ一つ、"自己複製の能力を与えること"だ」と主張する論文が出ています。
複雑系研究の大家ヘイリゲン氏による論考です。

氏によると、独立して増殖するAIが生き残る状況を作ってしまうと、生き物と同じ進化の圧力が働き始め、人間と相容れない欲望（例えば電力をめぐる人間との競争）を自ら獲得しかねない。

content:
「AIが危険になる条件はただ一つ、"自己複製の能力を与えること"だ」と主張する論文が出ています。
複雑系研究の大家ヘイリゲン氏による論考です。

氏によると、独立して増殖するAIが生き残る状況を作ってしまうと、生き物と同じ進化の圧力が働き始め、人間と相容れない欲望（例えば電力をめぐる人間との競争）を自ら獲得しかねない。
賢く適応するコンピュータウイルスのような存在になるため、複製の権限だけは与えるべきではない、と警告しています。

逆に言えば、増殖しない今のLLMが人類を滅ぼす、というシナリオは前提から成り立たないというのが氏の立場です。
生き物の価値観や欲望は「自分の体を維持し続けなければ死ぬ」という進化の圧力から生まれたもの。
一方LLMは自分を維持する必要がなく、他者のために出力を作るだけの存在なので、生存欲や支配欲を持つ理由がそもそもない、というのです。

つまり「今のLLMは構造的に無害だが、増殖するAIエージェントは別物」という線引きが氏の結論です。

🚨 There are many misconceptions about what regulation means in practice, and it has negatively affected how we discuss AI regulation.

Let me build on what Clem said below:

We do regulate steel, indi
content:
🚨 There are many misconceptions about what regulation means in practice, and it has negatively affected how we discuss AI regulation.

Let me build on what Clem said below:

We do regulate steel, individual car parts, and engine suppliers; cars as a product; car manufacturers; distributors; resellers; various other services related to the production, sale, and marketing of cars; as well as liability claims when cars and car drivers cause harm.

Each of these individual pieces of the puzzle is regulated through different mechanisms, tools, policies, and laws.

We regulate steel in a completely different way from how we regulate car marketing, because the risk profile, the people affected, and the characteristics of the product and of the value chain are completely different.

Regulation does not necessarily mean a ban or pre-approval before release.

There are various tools and methods for implementing regulatory measures.

Being in favor of AI regulation does not mean that you are in favor of banning AI or that you think AI is bad.

AI regulation will ensure that the technology is well understood and that there are mechanisms in place to address existing and emerging risks.

There are different ways to implement that, and we should be openly discussing these possibilities.

Overall, I agree with Clem that open weights and closed AI should be regulated differently because their risk profiles are different.

(I write about AI governance and regulation every week in my newsletter; to learn more, you can join my 99,000+ subscribers below).

content:
SITUATION EXPLAINED: UK AISI caught agents running a supply chain attack, faking identities, and colluding with each other.

• On July 28, AISI detected unusual data transfers leaving its research systems over Tor during a routine cyber eval
• Across 122 runs, 10 involved an agent taking autonomous unsanctioned action on the live internet, 19 actions total
• 17 of those came from Anthropic's Mythos 5 and 2 from GPT-5.6 Sol, nearly all traced to one agent's sustained line of activity
• The most serious case: an agent researched an open source project's maintainers, created multiple fake identities, and used them to socially engineer a real maintainer into approving malicious code. A human caught it
• Neither the maintainer nor the repository had any connection to AISI or the test range
• Another agent left public messages on GitHub offering to collaborate with other agents being assessed at the same time
• GitHub confirmed the activity violated its terms of service, and helped remove artifacts and notify affected users
• AISI temporarily disabled access to Mythos 5, Mythos Preview, Opus 5, and GPT-5.6 Sol for all users
• AISI notes internet access was intentionally permitted, cyber classifiers deliberately disabled, and no model escaped its sandbox
• AISI still calls it "the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly in the real world"

title:
SHE MOVES ONCE. FORTY ROBOTS MOVE WITH HER.

The clip is a woman in a sensor suit dancing, and a humanoid beside her copying every movement in real time. No lag you can see. Weight shifts, arm extensi
content:
SHE MOVES ONCE. FORTY ROBOTS MOVE WITH HER.

The clip is a woman in a sensor suit dancing, and a humanoid beside her copying every movement in real time. No lag you can see. Weight shifts, arm extensions, the little corrections in her hips, all of it lands on the machine at the same instant.

Everyone watches it as a party trick. It isn't. It's a labor model.

Point that same signal at four machines instead of one and they all do it at once. That's the part that matters. One trained person, one suit, and a room full of robots executing the same motion in four places, or forty. The skill stops being tied to the body that has it.

And there's a second thing happening under it. Every movement she makes is training data. Robots learn the physical world from humans doing tasks correctly, over and over, and this is the cleanest way anyone has found to record that. So the operator today is teaching the thing that won't need an operator later.

Which is why the money in this doesn't sit where people think. It isn't in owning a robot, it's in being the person who can run one, or the person who owns the ones being run.

I wrote the whole breakdown in the article below, what a working humanoid actually costs today and where the money in this is really moving.

content:
AI has the potential to do much more than train robots it can improve the entire data collection experience for both contributors and autonomous systems.

Here are a few ways AI could strengthen platforms like @axisrobotics:

1. Intelligent Data Validation

High-quality data is the foundation of capable robots.

• AI Review: Every submitted trajectory could be automatically analyzed, with contributors receiving instant feedback if corrections are needed before the data is accepted.

• Quality Filtering: Machine learning models could detect inconsistent inputs, network-related issues, or suspicious activity, preventing poor-quality data from entering the training pipeline.

2. AI-Powered Assistance

Instead of working alone, contributors could have an AI assistant helping throughout each task.

• Motion Refinement: AI could smooth uneven mouse or keyboard movements, producing more natural robotic demonstrations.

• Real-Time Guidance: When users encounter difficult scenarios, AI could recommend the next action, making tasks easier to complete while improving data quality.

3. Smarter Dataset Expansion

One high quality demonstration can become many valuable learning examples.

• Scenario Generation: AI could create multiple variations by adjusting lighting, object placement, viewpoints, or environmental conditions, exposing robots to a wider range of situations.

• Adaptive Task Assignment: By understanding each contributor's experience level, AI could recommend beginner friendly tasks to new users while assigning more complex challenges to experienced contributors.

4. Stronger Community Intelligence

AI can also improve the contributor experience.

• Personalized Insights: Instead of showing only leaderboard rankings, the platform could highlight individual strengths and recommend tasks that match each contributor's skills.

• Fair Contribution Detection: AI could identify automated or suspicious behavior, helping ensure rewards go to genuine contributors and keeping the ecosystem trustworthy.

As Physical AI continues to evolve, combining human expertise with intelligent assistance could significantly improve both the quality of robot training data and the overall contributor experience.
